title: SUSTAINABLE 3D-PRINTED ACTIVE AND PASSIVE RF COMPONENTS FOR ANTENNA ARRAY APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and demonstrate 3D-printed active and passive RF components for L-band antenna arrayapplications, enabling more sustainable manufacturing and system integration.Description:The environmental impact of space activities is receiving increasing attention across the European spacesector. In line with ESA's Ecodesign Policy, future missions are expected to assess their environmentalfootprint through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and identify and implement solutions that reduce resourceconsumption, energy usage, waste generation, and hazardous materials. RF hardware is a particularly relevant target for ecodesign improvements due to its widespread deployment across satellite payloads and user terminals. Given the large number of RF components typically integrated within phased-array antenna architectures, even incremental reductions in environmental impacts at component level can translate into significant cumulative benefits at system and programme level.Phased Array Antennas (PAAs) are a key enabling technology for next-generation communications,navigation, and sensing systems, providing electronically steerable beams, enhanced reliability, andoperational flexibility. Conventional PAA manufacturing relies on complex and resource-intensive productionprocesses. Additive manufacturing, and in particular 3D printing, offers a sustainable alternative approachthrough the use of functional polymers and carbon-nanotube-based materials while reducing waste, energyusage, water consumption, and chemical processing.While significant progress has been achieved for passive RF components, the development of active RFdevices, particularly RF transistors, remains a key challenge and a barrier to fully 3D-printed RF systems. The ESA Discovery activity "GHz Organic Printed Transistors" (GHioza) demonstrated sustainable 3D-printed transistor technology up to approximately 300 MHz which is state of the art but not sufficient for phase-array antenna applications. The activity aims to develop sustainably manufactured 3D-printed RF transistorsoperating in L-band (1-2 GHz) and integrate them with antenna elements on a common substrate,demonstrating the co-integration of active and passive RF functionality within a unified additively manufacturedplatform. A proof-of-concept active array demonstrator comprising two to three antenna elements andassociated active circuitry will then be developed, with electronic beam steering demonstrated using anexternal Software Defined Radio for beamforming and phase control.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- requirements analysis- material characterization- RF transistor design- antenna/component co-integration- additive manufacturing process development- prototype fabrication- RF testing and validation- beam-steering demonstrations- development plan- Simplified LCA analysis and Ecodesign trade off and selection.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: ORGANIC MATERIALS USED IN LAUNCHERS APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To establish a de-risking strategy for the non-European dependency for organic materials such as silicones,elastomers, glues, resins for thermal protections for launchers applications.Description:In 2025, European chemistry faces critical challenges due to structural crises, industrial site closures, andintense international competition. Many groups in Europe and outside of Europe are reorganizing theirproduction, closing plants, or relocating to more competitive regions like Asia. Between 2019 and 2023,Europe's chemical production fell by 12%, with closure of over 20 industrial sites. In addition, groups must faceevolutions of regulations (e.g. REACH), monitoring and anticipating future forbidden substances (Substancesof Very High Concern - SVHC) and focus newinvestments on green chemistry and decarbonization viabiosourced molecules, recycling, and carbon capture. For example, PFAS regulation will be effective at leastby end of 2028, and a huge number of products will be forbidden, and aeronautic and aerospace sectors willbe severely impacted. For silicones some non-European suppliers informed that a supply risk exists for someolder references.The qualification of these applications is long and complex. Silicones are used in componentsin the manufacture of thermal protection to contribute for maintaining the shape and the flexibility of the thermalprotection. They also allow to stick and join components, respecting the thermal sealing.Other materials / use cases in the scope of this activity include:- Elastomers: Used in solidengines as a gas protection Procured outside Europe- Glues and Thread lock: Many parts of launcher, from structural materials to-Thread locks, need specific glues.- Resins: Solid Rocket Motor parts are manufactured using resin (bearing reinforcement material or the RTMinjection moulding process).- Aluminium adhesives: Used to maintain an electrically grounded connection of the thermal protections inESR (Thermal Protection, Thermal Cap Capture System, Mechanical Anti-Pitching System and RodThermal Protection).Thisactivity aims at implementing and supporting when required a multi-sourcing strategy withphysicochemical characterizations of proposedalternatives.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Assessment of requirements available from European launcher manufacturers,- Analysis of supply resilience and competitiveness for alternative products to answer Launchers needs inEurope (and other markers), including if required dual or triple source to limit impacts of specific policy ofeach other,- Physical and chemical characterisation of substitute materials (if no data available) to confirm suitabilitywith launcher requirements.- Make available and regularly update a catalogue of characterised alternative chemicals for Europeanmanufacturers.Deliverables: Other, Report

title: GT17-670GD - EVOLVED OPERATIONAL USER INTERFACES (EXPRO+)
description: Existing operational user interfaces for ground segment are primarily built on aging software platforms characterized by deprecated technologies, a monolithic architecture and rigid implementation. While these legacy platforms provide stability for established scenarios, it struggles to adapt to modern operational demands specifically the introduction of remote operations, cloud infrastructure management, and the seamless integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Building on the EGS-CC WebUI and the PulseUI, a specialized WebUI branch tailored for operational environments, the new approach has enabled support for comprehensive UI testing, facilitate remote control capabilities, and better align with the microservices architecture backends. To overcome these challenges and achieve the goals of the project, an architectural and design approach based on the following will be required: - Web-Based Architecture: To guarantee high flexibility and stability. - Unified Design System: Establishing a common look and feel across the ground segment.  - Industry-Standard Framework Principles: Adopting the principles of established UI frameworks (such as Material Design). This will provide a comprehensive suite of reusable components, complete with intuitive documentation and tutorials, hence mitigates the risk of "technology islands".

title: GREEK NATIONAL SATELLITE SPACE PROJECT - SPACE DOMAIN AWARENESS IN-ORBIT SERVICING (ISOS) PILLAR 2 - PHASE A/B1
description: As part of the Greek National Satellite Space Project - Phase 2, the objective of this activity is the procurement of Phase A/B1 for an In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) mission aimed at the development and in-space demonstration of a flexible small-satellite platformenabling future In-Space Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing (ISAM) missions.The mission shall demonstrate autonomous rendezvous,inspection and close-proximity operations (CPO) capabilities in orbit, while supporting the development of European industrial andcommercial capabilities and fostering future operational services.The mission shall address identified user needs and market opportunities with the objective of contributing to the development of future European in-space infrastructure and services. Tenderers shall therefore propose a mission concept that combines technology demonstration objectives with a credible path towards future operational applications.The mission and system development approach shall be based on a modular and scalable architecture, supported byanincremental demonstration strategy with clearly defined primary and extended objectives. The proposed implementation shall prioritise mission success, schedule robustness and affordability, while enabling future capability growth. Primary objectives will focus on demonstrating autonomous rendezvous, inspection and close-proximity operations capabilities, including relative navigation, guidance and control, onboard autonomy, mission operations and payload-carrying capability. Secondary objectives may include extended CPO manoeuvres (V-bar and R-bar approaches), synchronised relative motion demonstrations, technology maturation activities for futureISAM missions, and payload accommodation demonstrations such as advanced sensors or robotics. The implementation of secondary objectives will be subject to available resources and mission opportunities, without compromising the achievement of the primary objectives.
